about: The Quackenbush Still House was Albany’s first distillery, founded in the mid-18th century a short distance from where Albany Distilling Company opened in 2011. The company, started by teachers John Curtin and Matthew Jager and now owned by Curtin and Rick Sicari, named its rum for that predecessor and bills itself as the first licensed distillery in the city since Prohibition. Its spirits are made in small batches in Albany, with production now in a larger building on Third Street.

The Original Albany Rum follows the old still house’s recipe and methods, with modern equipment, better yeast and a cleaner water supply. It starts with fancy-grade Caribbean molasses, is distilled on a hybrid pot-and-column still and is bottled unaged at 40% alcohol, or 80 proof, with no added color or flavoring. Rested in used Ironweed whiskey barrels, the same spirit becomes the company’s Amber Rum.

Because it sees no barrel, the glass shows the molasses and the still directly. The distributor’s notes describe an earthy character in the Original, which time in oak later smooths into something subtler and warmer in the Amber. Unaged rum like this is the traditional base for a daiquiri or a mojito, drinks in which the rum’s own character has nowhere to hide.
